ballad.title: The Week on the Quays
verses: Now hear the news from quay and square,
The Schelde rose, the Schelde fell,
As it has done since time began.
And that's the truth, or near enough.
Another tale I have to tell,
The Schelde rose, the Schelde fell,
As it has done since time began.
And that's the truth, or near enough.
chorus: Oh the fog on the river, the rain on the quay,
there's news in the town for a centime from me.

sermon: Beloved in the Lord, I have heard more this week than a priest likes to hear.
Keep the Sabbath holy, and your hands in your own pockets.
Work honestly, drink little, and remember the poor at your door.
Honour your father and your mother, even when they are wrong.
The fog comes up the Schelde every morning, and still the ships find their way. So may you.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

A house burned,
The smoke rose black above the roofs,

Another tale I have to tell,

verses: Another tale I have to tell,
The Schelde rose, the Schelde fell,
As it has done since time began.
So God be good to all of us.

The Schelde rose, the Schelde fell,
As it has done since time began.
So God be good to all of us.
chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,
Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

facts.text: A house burned (near the quay); everybody escaped.
The town had news of robbery.

ballad.title: News from the Schelde
verses: Another tale I have to tell,
A house burned,
The smoke rose black above the roofs,
And buckets ran from hand to hand.
Come listen, dockers, wives and all,
The town had news of robbery,
A purse was lifted in the crowd,
And that's the truth, or near enough.
chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,
Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

sermon: My brothers and sisters in Christ, this week our town has given the devil good sport.
A house burned in our streets. Let it remind you how quickly all we hold can turn to ash, and look to your souls as to your chimneys.
Purses were lifted in our open streets. Thou shalt not steal: it was not written for the rich alone.
Keep the Sabbath holy, and your hands in your own pockets.
Work honestly, drink little, and remember the poor at your door.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

verses: Another tale I have to tell,
Jef helped at the quay,
The farm boy Jef was in it too,
And half the quay was there to see.
Come listen, dockers, wives and all,

A ship came in upon the tide,

Come gather round, good people all,

The bells rang out, the guests made merry,
And that's the truth, or near enough.

verses: Come listen, dockers, wives and all,
The Schelde rose, the Schelde fell,
As it has done since time began.
So mind your purse and mind your way.
Come gather round, good people all,
The Schelde rose, the Schelde fell,
As it has done since time began.
So mind your purse and mind your way.
chorus: Oh the fog on the river, the rain on the quay,
there's news in the town for a centime from me.

sermon: Beloved in the Lord, I have heard more this week than a priest likes to hear.
Keep the Sabbath holy, and your hands in your own pockets.
Work honestly, drink little, and remember the poor at your door.
Honour your father and your mother, even when they are wrong.
The fog comes up the Schelde every morning, and still the ships find their way. So may you.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

facts.text: A house burned (near the quay); everybody escaped.
The town had news of robbery.

ballad.title: News from the Schelde
verses: Another tale I have to tell,
A house burned,
The smoke rose black above the roofs,
And buckets ran from hand to hand.
Come listen, dockers, wives and all,
The town had news of robbery,
A purse was lifted in the crowd,
And that's the truth, or near enough.
chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,
Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

sermon: My brothers and sisters in Christ, this week our town has given the devil good sport.
A house burned in our streets. Let it remind you how quickly all we hold can turn to ash, and look to your souls as to your chimneys.

Keep the Sabbath holy, and your hands in your own pockets.
Work honestly, drink little, and remember the poor at your door.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

facts.text: The town had news of drink.
The town had news of emigrants.
The town had news of funeral.
The town had news of scuffle.

ballad.title: News from the Schelde
verses: Another tale I have to tell,
The town had news of drink,
The square was full, the talk was loud,
And everybody had a view.
Come listen, dockers, wives and all,
The town had news of emigrants,
They came with chests from far away,
To wait for ships to the new land.
Come gather round, good people all,
The town had news of funeral,
The bell went slow, the black cloth hung,
And all the street took off its hat.
chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,
Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

sermon: My brothers and sisters in Christ, this week our town has given the devil good sport.
The taverns did good trade and the families bad. Jenever warms the belly for an hour and chills the home for a week.
Strangers wait on our quays with their chests for the ship. Be kind to them; the Holy Family too were travellers.
We buried one of our own this week. Remember that none of us knows the hour.
Neighbours raised their voices and their hands in the market. Anger is a fire in a wooden house; do not feed it.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

facts.text: A house burned (near the quay); everybody escaped.
The town had news of robbery.

ballad.title: A New Song of the Town
verses: Come gather round, good people all,
A house burned,
The smoke rose black above the roofs,
And buckets ran from hand to hand.
Now hear the news from quay and square,
The town had news of robbery,
A purse was lifted in the crowd,
So mind your purse and mind your way.
chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,
Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

sermon: My brothers and sisters in Christ, this week our town has given the devil good sport.
A house burned in our streets. Let it remind you how quickly all we hold can turn to ash, and look to your souls as to your chimneys.
Purses were lifted in our open streets. Thou shalt not steal: it was not written for the rich alone.
Keep the Sabbath holy, and your hands in your own pockets.
Work honestly, drink little, and remember the poor at your door.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

ballad.title: The Farm Boy on the Quays
verses: Come gather round, good people all,
Jef helped at the quay,

Now hear the news from quay and square,

The bells rang out, the guests made merry,

chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,

facts.text: The town had news of drink.
The town had news of emigrants.
The town had news of funeral.
The town had news of scuffle.

ballad.title: A New Song of the Town
verses: Come gather round, good people all,
The town had news of drink,
The square was full, the talk was loud,
And everybody had a view.
Now hear the news from quay and square,
The town had news of emigrants,
They came with chests from far away,
To wait for ships to the new land.
Another tale I have to tell,
The town had news of funeral,
The bell went slow, the black cloth hung,
And all the street took off its hat.
chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,
Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

sermon: My brothers and sisters in Christ, this week our town has given the devil good sport.
The taverns did good trade and the families bad. Jenever warms the belly for an hour and chills the home for a week.
Strangers wait on our quays with their chests for the ship. Be kind to them; the Holy Family too were travellers.
We buried one of our own this week. Remember that none of us knows the hour.
Neighbours raised their voices and their hands in the market. Anger is a fire in a wooden house; do not feed it.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

verses: Now hear the news from quay and square,

Another tale I have to tell,

So keep your head, and pray for rain.
chorus: Oh the fog on the river, the rain on the quay,

sermon: Beloved in the Lord, I have heard more this week than a priest likes to hear.
A house burned in our streets. Let it remind you how quickly all we hold can turn to ash, and look to your souls as to your chimneys.
Purses were lifted in our open streets. Thou shalt not steal: it was not written for the rich alone.
Keep the Sabbath holy, and your hands in your own pockets.
Work honestly, drink little, and remember the poor at your door.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

facts.text: The town had news of drink.
The town had news of emigrants.
The town had news of funeral.
The town had news of scuffle.

ballad.title: The Week on the Quays
verses: Now hear the news from quay and square,
The town had news of drink,
The square was full, the talk was loud,
And everybody had a view.
Another tale I have to tell,
The town had news of emigrants,
They came with chests from far away,
To wait for ships to the new land.
Come listen, dockers, wives and all,
The town had news of funeral,
The bell went slow, the black cloth hung,
And all the street took off its hat.
chorus: Oh the fog on the river, the rain on the quay,
there's news in the town for a centime from me.

sermon: Beloved in the Lord, I have heard more this week than a priest likes to hear.
The taverns did good trade and the families bad. Jenever warms the belly for an hour and chills the home for a week.
Strangers wait on our quays with their chests for the ship. Be kind to them; the Holy Family too were travellers.
We buried one of our own this week. Remember that none of us knows the hour.
Neighbours raised their voices and their hands in the market. Anger is a fire in a wooden house; do not feed it.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

verses: Another tale I have to tell,

Come listen, dockers, wives and all,

chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,

ballad.title: The Farm Boy on the Quays
verses: Another tale I have to tell,
Jef helped at the quay,
The farm boy Jef was in it too,
And half the quay was there to see.
Come listen, dockers, wives and all,
The town had news of ship,
A ship came in upon the tide,

Come gather round, good people all,

The bells rang out, the guests made merry,
And that's the truth, or near enough.
chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,
Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

facts.text: The town had news of drink.
The town had news of emigrants.
The town had news of funeral.
The town had news of scuffle.

ballad.title: News from the Schelde
verses: Another tale I have to tell,
The town had news of drink,
The square was full, the talk was loud,
And everybody had a view.
Come listen, dockers, wives and all,
The town had news of emigrants,
They came with chests from far away,
To wait for ships to the new land.
Come gather round, good people all,
The town had news of funeral,
The bell went slow, the black cloth hung,
And all the street took off its hat.
chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,
Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

sermon: My brothers and sisters in Christ, this week our town has given the devil good sport.
The taverns did good trade and the families bad. Jenever warms the belly for an hour and chills the home for a week.
Strangers wait on our quays with their chests for the ship. Be kind to them; the Holy Family too were travellers.
We buried one of our own this week. Remember that none of us knows the hour.
Neighbours raised their voices and their hands in the market. Anger is a fire in a wooden house; do not feed it.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

facts.text: The town had news of drink.
The town had news of emigrants.
The town had news of funeral.
The town had news of scuffle.

ballad.title: A True and Merry Song
verses: Come listen, dockers, wives and all,
The town had news of drink,
The square was full, the talk was loud,
And everybody had a view.
Come gather round, good people all,
The town had news of emigrants,
They came with chests from far away,
To wait for ships to the new land.
Now hear the news from quay and square,
The town had news of funeral,
The bell went slow, the black cloth hung,
And all the street took off its hat.
chorus: Oh the fog on the river, the rain on the quay,
there's news in the town for a centime from me.

sermon: Beloved in the Lord, I have heard more this week than a priest likes to hear.
The taverns did good trade and the families bad. Jenever warms the belly for an hour and chills the home for a week.
Strangers wait on our quays with their chests for the ship. Be kind to them; the Holy Family too were travellers.
We buried one of our own this week. Remember that none of us knows the hour.
Neighbours raised their voices and their hands in the market. Anger is a fire in a wooden house; do not feed it.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

ballad.title: A New Song of the Town
verses: Come gather round, good people all,
The town had news of drink,
The square was full, the talk was loud,
And everybody had a view.
Now hear the news from quay and square,
The town had news of emigrants,
They came with chests from far away,
To wait for ships to the new land.
Another tale I have to tell,
The town had news of funeral,
The bell went slow, the black cloth hung,
And all the street took off its hat.
chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,
Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

sermon: My brothers and sisters in Christ, this week our town has given the devil good sport.
The taverns did good trade and the families bad. Jenever warms the belly for an hour and chills the home for a week.
Strangers wait on our quays with their chests for the ship. Be kind to them; the Holy Family too were travellers.
We buried one of our own this week. Remember that none of us knows the hour.
Neighbours raised their voices and their hands in the market. Anger is a fire in a wooden house; do not feed it.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

facts.text: The town had news of drink.

The town had news of funeral.
The town had news of scuffle.

ballad.title: The Week on the Quays
verses: Now hear the news from quay and square,
The town had news of drink,
The square was full, the talk was loud,
And everybody had a view.
Another tale I have to tell,
The town had news of emigrants,
They came with chests from far away,
To wait for ships to the new land.
Come listen, dockers, wives and all,
The town had news of funeral,
The bell went slow, the black cloth hung,
And all the street took off its hat.
chorus: Oh the fog on the river, the rain on the quay,
there's news in the town for a centime from me.

sermon: Beloved in the Lord, I have heard more this week than a priest likes to hear.
The taverns did good trade and the families bad. Jenever warms the belly for an hour and chills the home for a week.
Strangers wait on our quays with their chests for the ship. Be kind to them; the Holy Family too were travellers.
We buried one of our own this week. Remember that none of us knows the hour.
Neighbours raised their voices and their hands in the market. Anger is a fire in a wooden house; do not feed it.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.

The Schelde rose, the Schelde fell,
As it has done since time began.
So God be good to all of us.

The Schelde rose, the Schelde fell,

Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

ballad.title: News from the Schelde
verses: Another tale I have to tell,
The town had news of drink,
The square was full, the talk was loud,
And everybody had a view.
Come listen, dockers, wives and all,
The town had news of emigrants,
They came with chests from far away,
To wait for ships to the new land.
Come gather round, good people all,
The town had news of funeral,
The bell went slow, the black cloth hung,
And all the street took off its hat.
chorus: Sing hey for the Schelde, sing ho for the fog,
Antwerp keeps singing whatever may come.

sermon: My brothers and sisters in Christ, this week our town has given the devil good sport.
The taverns did good trade and the families bad. Jenever warms the belly for an hour and chills the home for a week.
Strangers wait on our quays with their chests for the ship. Be kind to them; the Holy Family too were travellers.
We buried one of our own this week. Remember that none of us knows the hour.
Neighbours raised their voices and their hands in the market. Anger is a fire in a wooden house; do not feed it.
Go in peace, and may Our Lady keep the fog from your hearts. Amen.
